title: American Academy of Periodontology Installs Dr. Kristi M. Soileau as President
html:
New Orleans periodontist to lead during the 2026–2027 term

Media Contact: Adam Natali, American Academy of Periodontology
Phone: 312-573-3240 | Email: [email protected]

CHICAGO — November 10, 2026 — The American Academy of Periodontology (AAP) has installed Kristi M. Soileau, DDS, MEd, MSHCE, as its president for the 2026–2027 term. Dr. Soileau began her term on Oct. 31, 2026, at the AAP Annual Meeting in Seattle.

A board-certified periodontist in private practice in New Orleans, Dr. Soileau brings extensive experience in clinical care, dental education, professional leadership, and health care ethics to her presidency.

Dr. Soileau earned her dental degree from the LSU School of Dentistry in 1985, followed by certificates in Advanced Education in General Dentistry in 1986 and Periodontics in 1988. She also earned a Master of Education from the University of New Orleans in 1987 and a Master of Science in Health Care Ethics from Creighton University in 2017.

“Giving back has long been central to my work, from volunteering as a dentist for Notre Dame Hospice to spending decades in nursing home dentistry,” Dr. Soileau states. “Throughout my career, I have encouraged colleagues to bring that commitment to their own communities. As AAP president, I plan to bring that same dedication and energy to my term.”

Dr. Soileau is a gratis part-time clinical associate professor in the Periodontal Postdoctoral Program at the LSU School of Dentistry, which named her Alumna of the Year in 2016. Her leadership roles have included president of the New Orleans Dental Association, the Louisiana Dental Association, and the LSU School of Dentistry Alumni Association Board of Directors. She has served as Editor for the New Orleans Dental Association since 1988 and is past Chair-Elect of the LSU Health Foundation Board. She previously served as president of the Southwest Society of Periodontists.

Dr. Soileau’s national professional service includes the American Dental Association’s Council on Ethics, Bylaws and Judicial Affairs, the Council on Dental Education and Licensure, and over a decade on the ADA House of Delegates. She is the Louisiana Deputy Regent of the International College of Dentists, a member of the Pierre Fauchard Academy, and a past Area 6 Regent for the American College of Dentists.

About the AAP
The American Academy of Periodontology (AAP) is a 6,500-member professional organization for periodontists – specialists in the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases affecting the gums and supporting structures of the teeth, and in the placement of dental implants. Periodontists are also dentistry’s experts in the treatment of oral inflammation and receive three additional years of specialized training following dental school. Periodontics is one of the 12 dental specialties recognized by the American Dental Association.
